title: Hushwave: region-aware alert noise-gating, failover runbook, and automated incident responder
creator: Marco Rivera
description: Reduce noisy pager churn during transient multiregion degradations by implementing a region-aware alert noise gate ('Hushwave'), coordinated circuit-breaker windowing, and an automated failover responder. The goal is to preserve SLO observability and mean time to mitigate for real incidents while preventing paging for low-signal, high-noise events (e.g., short-lived region flaps, cache warmups, or transient GPU scheduling spikes).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Pager volume for page-level 'region-degraded' signals drops >= 70% for simulated transient flaps while true-positives for sustained degradations remain >= 95%
2) Automated failover can transition traffic between primary and secondary regions within defined SLO windows without manual escalation (time-to-traffic-shift <= 120s under test),
3) Circuit-breaker windowing prevents overload cascade: downstream tail latency spikes reduced by >= 60% in synthetic overload tests
4) Runbook invocation is audited and produces a timeline entry in the incident dashboard; automated steps can be manually overridden by on-call
5) Implementation includes a documented kill-switch (feature flag) and telemetry page for rollout observability
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Design - finalize gating heuristics (window length, score thresholds) and list of signals used (region error-rate, per-model p50/p95 latency delta, KV-cache miss spike, instance churn)
Phase 2: Proof-of-concept - implement hushwave scoring service as a lightweight sidecar that subscribes to alert streams and emits 'suppress' or 'escalate' decisions
Phase 3: Automation - wire decisions into PagerDuty routing + runtime control plane to execute failover (traffic-shift API) and circuit-breaker adjustments
Phase 4: Simulations - run fault-injection and chaos experiments across staging and ded-labs (including multi-region packet loss and cold-start scenarios)
Phase 5: Rollout - gradual canary (10% of routes), monitor key metrics, expand to 50% then 100% with post-rollout review
Owners: Aisha (runtime control), Sam Cho (observability), Priya Nair (oncall/runbooks), Marco (overall)
Implementation PRs: GH#redwood/runtime PRs: 4832 (hushwave-score), 4861 (control-plane wiring), 4877 (runbook UI hooks)
metrics_and_thresholds: SLOs in scope: 99th-percentile token latency <= 800ms for api.gen.* across regions; availability SLO 99.95% per-region

Hushwave scoring inputs: 60s sliding window error-rate delta > 2x baseline (weight 3), p95 latency delta > 1.8x (weight 2), KV-cache miss-rate spike > 1.5x (weight 1.5), recent instance churn > 3% (weight 1)
Score threshold: suppress if composite score between 1.0-2.5 (noise window), escalate if > 2.5 and sustained for > 90s
Circuit-breaker windowing: progressive thresholds at 30s/90s/300s with increasing load-shedding percentages 10%/30%/60%
Alert dedupe and grouping: group by route/model/region over 45s correlation window before paging
Telemetry: track suppressed_count, suppression_true_positive_rate, failover_latency, client-side error spikes post-failover
runbook_snippets: When primary-region p95 > 1.8x baseline AND hushwave score > 2.5 for > 90s: 1) Confirm 'hushwave' dashboard (link) 2) Trigger automated traffic-shift (control-plane API) to next healthy region at 20% increments every 30s with health-check gating 3) Monitor client error-rate and p99 latency; if improve, continue; else roll back
If automated failover fails to reach stable health after 3 increments: escalate to on-call leader and open incident channel #ops-multiregion
Circuit-breaker manual override: set route.circuit.mode = 'open' to enforce 60% shed for route; document change in incident timeline and include reason and expected recovery time
Post-incident checklist: collect runtime logs (last 30m), upload relevant dashboards, run quick regression evals against canary requests, schedule follow-up retro
automation_playflows: Playflow A (Noise suppression): hushwave score computed by stream processor -> if in noise window, annotate alerts as 'suppressed' in AlertManager and add suppression entry to incident log (auto tickets suppressed in PD)
Playflow B (Autofailover): once score > escalate threshold and health probes fail, trigger traffic-shift via control-plane API with canary steps and automated rollback on probe failure
Playflow C (Circuit-windowing): when overload detected, progressively apply per-route shedding policies and notify on-call with actionable buttons (apply, revert, escalate)
All flows produce an immutable audit record with correlation ID and store a snapshot of contributing signals in S3/GS for later analysis (see links)
rollout_plan: Week 0: Feature flag behind ff.hushwave.rollout and ff.controlplane.autofailover; enable in staging for 100% of routes
Week 1: Canary in production - enable for low-traffic routes (10%) and run 3 black-box tests and 5 chaos scenarios
Week 2: Expand to 50% of routes after sign-off from SRE and Product; run scheduled tabletop incident drill with on-call
Week 3: Full production rollout with 24/7 monitor window and rotation of on-call members watching hushwave dashboard
Fallback: Immediate feature-flag disable and manual traffic reversion scripts documented in runbook

postmortem_notes: From last incident sim: false suppression occurred once when bulk KV-cache miss was caused by deployment job; mitigation: add deployment-context signal to suppress scoring
Runbook clarity: add explicit escalation TTLs and ownership (who should be paged after automated steps fail)
Observability: capture pre-suppression traces for first-failure analysis; we currently sample too sparsely
